preconditions.expression: len(good_letters) >= 1 and len(good_letters) <= 26 and all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in good_letters) and len(set(good_letters)) == len(good_letters)
preconditions.description: The first line is a string of distinct lowercase English letters (good_letters) with length between 1 and 26.

preconditions.expression: len(pattern) >= 1 and len(pattern) <= 10**5 and all(c.islower() or c in {'?', '*'} for c in pattern) and pattern.count('*') <= 1
preconditions.description: The second line is a pattern string (pattern) of length 1 to 10^5, containing lowercase letters, '?', and at most one '*' character.
The third line is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of query strings.

preconditions.expression: all(len(query) >= 1 and all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in query) for query in queries)
preconditions.description: The next n lines are non-empty strings (queries) of lowercase English letters, with total length across all queries ≤ 10^5.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == n and all(line in {'YES', 'NO'} for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly n lines, each containing either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive).

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i] == 'YES') == matches_pattern(queries[i], good_letters, pattern) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each query string queries[i], output_lines[i] is 'YES' if and only if the pattern matches the query string according to the rules: '?' can be replaced by any good letter, and '*' (if present) can be replaced by any string of bad letters (including empty).
